name: SyncHarbor
title: Reviewable REST Data Synchronization
problem: Manual data transfers make changes hard to inspect and recover from when paginated API records differ from the saved dataset.
solution: A working REST-to-SQLite pipeline with dot-path mapping, review before commit, explicit update approval and reversible snapshots.
features: Real paginated HTTP fetches with field mapping
Add/change/conflict review and optimistic revision checks
Atomic SQLite commits and recovery snapshots
CSV/JSON export with spreadsheet-safe CSV values
verification: 9 automated tests passed, including actual loopback HTTP pagination, approved updates, stale-preview rejection, exports and reversible restores.
limitations: New independent project; fictional verification data. Single-user local service; documented items/next JSON envelope. Remote endpoints require explicit opt-in; OAuth, scheduled sync and public deployment are not implemented.
flow: HTTP JSON source → Pagination & mapping → Addition/change review → Explicit commit → SQLite snapshot → CSV/JSON export
captions: Two-page HTTP source and field mapping in the real SyncHarbor workspace.
A revised source produces one addition and two modifications against saved records, ready for explicit review before commit.
